<thought>We have a ¹H NMR spectrum showing a single aromatic signal at 7.51 ppm integrating to 10 protons (dddd). This suggests an aromatic hydrocarbon with ten equivalent aromatic hydrogens. The simplest such formula is C₁₄H₁₀ (anthracene, phenanthrene, etc.). To identify the exact structure while conserving resources, the next cheapest informative experiment is mass spectrometry to obtain the molecular ion mass, which will confirm the molecular formula. Once we have the formula, we can retrieve possible isomers and select the one that matches the NMR pattern (a single aromatic resonance). This approach avoids unnecessary full‑spectra simulations.</thought>
